title: Lexing and Unescaping String Literals
description: Scan double-quoted string literals containing escape sequences, decode escapes in a single pass, and observe how an unterminated string hits MISMATCH.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: Line 10 adds `("STRING", r'"(?:[^"\\]|\\.)*"')` to `TOKEN_SPEC`. Inside the outer quotes `"..."`, the non-capturing group `(?:[^"\\]|\\.)*` matches zero or more repetitions of either a safe character (`[^"\\]`, neither quote nor backslash) or a two-character escape sequence (`\\.`).

`tokenize(source)` yields `Token` objects and raises `SyntaxError` on `"MISMATCH"`. `unescape(raw)` slices off the surrounding quotes with `raw[1:-1]` (line 45) and uses `re.sub(r"\\(.)", ...)` (line 46) to decode every `\x` escape in one left-to-right pass using `ESCAPES`.

Compare `unescape(path)` (line 70) with chained `.replace("\\\\", "\\").replace("\\n", "\n")` (line 71) on `r'"c:\\new"'`: `re.sub` consumes `\\` in one pass and never rescans the replacement `\` together with the following `n`.
Lines 48-65 tokenize `program` (containing plain, escaped-quote, and `\n` strings) and print both the raw lexemes and unescaped Python strings, and lines 67-71 run the `r'"c:\\new"'` comparison.

steps.question: When `list(tokenize('let x = "oops;'))` runs on line 80, there is no closing quote. Which rule in `TOKEN_SPEC` matches at column 9 (`"`), and what exception is raised?
steps.answer: Because `STRING` requires a closing `"`, `"` at column 9 fails `STRING` and falls through to `MISMATCH` (`r"."`), raising `SyntaxError: line 1, col 9: unexpected '"'`.

steps.description: Lines 77-85 run `tokenize('let x = "oops;')` and catch the `SyntaxError` raised when the opening quote falls through to `MISMATCH`.
Inside `unescape('"hello, world"')`, line 45 has stripped the outer quotes to `'hello, world'` and line 46 runs the single-pass `re.sub`.
